primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Chronic acid reflux can cause metaplasia of distal esophageal squamous epithelium to intestinal-type columnar epithelium with goblet cells, increasing adenocarcinoma risk.
vignette: A 55-year-old man with long-standing GERD undergoes endoscopy. Distal esophageal biopsy shows columnar epithelium with goblet cells.
correct: Intestinal metaplasia of esophageal squamous epithelium
distractor_notes: Barrett requires metaplastic intestinal-type columnar epithelium.
Gastric epithelial change alone does not define Barrett esophagus.
Acute necrosis is not the chronic adaptive lesion.
Smooth-muscle hypertrophy is not the key epithelial change.
key_expl: Barrett esophagus is intestinal metaplasia caused by chronic reflux injury.
objective: Identify intestinal metaplasia in Barrett esophagus.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Chronic GERD and Barrett metaplasia predispose to adenocarcinoma of the distal esophagus, presenting with progressive dysphagia and weight loss.
vignette: A 62-year-old man with obesity and Barrett esophagus develops progressive dysphagia first to solids and later liquids with weight loss.
distractor_notes: Achalasia causes dysphagia to solids and liquids from the start and bird-beak narrowing.
Squamous carcinoma is associated more strongly with tobacco/alcohol and often arises in the mid-esophagus.
Peptic ulcer disease does not cause progressive mechanical dysphagia.
Diffuse spasm causes intermittent chest pain and dysphagia, not progressive obstruction with weight loss.
key_expl: Progressive mechanical dysphagia in a patient with Barrett esophagus strongly suggests distal esophageal adenocarcinoma.
objective: Recognize esophageal adenocarcinoma risk factors and presentation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells and intrinsic factor causes vitamin B12 malabsorption and can produce achlorhydria and megaloblastic anemia.
vignette: A 67-year-old woman has macrocytic anemia, paresthesias, positive anti-intrinsic-factor antibodies, and achlorhydria.
lead: Which gastric cell type is primarily targeted?
distractor_notes: Chief cells secrete pepsinogen.
G cells secrete gastrin.
D cells secrete somatostatin.
Paneth cells are intestinal crypt cells.
key_expl: Parietal cells produce intrinsic factor and hydrochloric acid; autoimmune loss causes pernicious anemia and achlorhydria.
objective: Identify parietal-cell loss in pernicious anemia.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Dietary iron is absorbed mainly in the duodenum and proximal jejunum; hepcidin regulates ferroportin-mediated export into plasma.
vignette: A patient undergoes resection of the duodenum and proximal jejunum.
lead: Which nutrient deficiency is most likely to develop?
distractors: Vitamin K from colonic bacteria only
distractor_notes: Vitamin B12 is absorbed in the terminal ileum.
Bile acids are reabsorbed mainly in terminal ileum.
Vitamin K deficiency is not specifically caused by proximal small-bowel resection.
Copper is absorbed largely in the stomach and proximal small intestine, but iron is the classic major nutrient lost with duodenal resection.
key_expl: Iron absorption occurs predominantly in the duodenum and proximal jejunum.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Most conjugated bile acids are actively reabsorbed in the terminal ileum and returned to the liver through enterohepatic circulation.
vignette: A patient with Crohn disease undergoes extensive terminal ileal resection and develops chronic watery diarrhea and fat malabsorption.
lead: Loss of which normal process most directly contributes?
correct: Active reabsorption of bile acids in the terminal ileum
distractors: Intrinsic factor secretion by parietal cells
distractor_notes: Iron absorption is proximal small bowel.
Intrinsic factor is secreted by stomach.
Pancreatic enzyme secretion occurs in pancreas.
Bile-acid malabsorption specifically follows terminal ileal disease.
key_expl: The terminal ileum recycles bile acids; loss reduces bile salt pool and sends bile acids into colon, causing diarrhea.
objective: Explain consequences of terminal ileal resection.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Many sporadic colorectal cancers develop through sequential genetic alterations including APC loss, KRAS activation, and later TP53 pathway disruption.
vignette: A colonic adenoma acquires additional mutations and progresses toward invasive adenocarcinoma.
lead: Which tumor suppressor is commonly lost early in the conventional adenoma-carcinoma pathway?
distractor_notes: RET activation causes MEN2.
VHL loss predisposes to clear-cell RCC and other tumors.
WT1 abnormalities are associated with Wilms tumor.
NF2 loss causes schwannomas and meningiomas.
key_expl: APC loss is an early driver of the conventional colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence.
objective: Identify APC as an early colorectal tumor-suppressor loss.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma often arises in the head of the pancreas and can obstruct the common bile duct, causing painless jaundice, dark urine, pale stools, and weight loss.
vignette: A 70-year-old man has painless progressive jaundice, weight loss, dark urine, pale stools, and a palpable nontender gallbladder.
distractor_notes: Cholecystitis causes painful RUQ inflammation.
Hepatitis A causes hepatocellular illness rather than painless obstructive jaundice with gallbladder enlargement.
Gilbert syndrome causes mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia without cholestatic stool/urine changes.
Peptic ulcer disease does not cause obstructive jaundice.
key_expl: Painless obstructive jaundice with weight loss and a palpable gallbladder strongly suggests pancreatic head cancer.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Gastrin from antral G cells stimulates gastric acid secretion largely through enterochromaffin-like cell histamine release and trophic effects on gastric mucosa.
vignette: Antral G cells are stimulated after a protein-rich meal.
lead: Which gastric secretion increases most directly downstream?
distractor_notes: Parietal cells secrete both acid and intrinsic factor, but gastrin is classically linked to increased acid secretion.
Pancreatic bicarbonate is primarily stimulated by secretin.
Bile release is strongly influenced by CCK.
Colonic mucus is not the main gastrin target.
key_expl: Gastrin promotes acid secretion directly and indirectly through histamine from ECL cells.
objective: Identify the principal gastric effect of gastrin.
